accelerator:ags.summary_technical: Brookhaven's Alternating Gradient Synchrotron, commissioned in 1960 using the strong-focusing (alternating-gradient) principle invented there; reached a design energy of 33 GeV for protons. Now serves as part of the injector chain that accelerates protons and heavy ions before delivery to the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider.

notes: kind is recorded as `linac`; CEBAF is technically a recirculating (racetrack) superconducting linac, which ACCELERATOR_KINDS does not have a dedicated value for.

2026-09-17: added CEBAF's original operating history (first beam 1994-07-01, 4 GeV design energy 1995, 6 GeV 'enhanced design energy' 2000-08-06) from src:jlab-wikipedia, which the prior session had already cited but had not mined beyond the 1987 construction-start and 2018 12 GeV-dedication dates (RESEARCH_AGENT_RULES.md #8: give the richest sourced history).
accelerator:cebaf.summary_technical: Continuous Electron Beam Accelerator Facility: a superconducting recirculating (racetrack) electron linac at Jefferson Lab; first beam 1994-07-01, reached its 4 GeV design energy in 1995, an 'enhanced design energy' of 6 GeV in 2000, and 12 GeV after the Upgrade dedicated 2018-05-02.

accelerator:fermilab-booster.summary_technical: 474 m circumference rapid-cycling synchrotron running at 15 Hz, accelerating protons from 400 MeV to 8 GeV kinetic energy (8.89 GeV/c) for the BNB and for injection into the Recycler and Main Injector.

accelerator:fermilab-linac.summary_technical: 201.25 MHz normal-conducting H- linac delivering 400 MeV to the Booster; to be replaced by the 800 MeV PIP-II superconducting linac.

notes: Design energy 150 GeV per the NuMI beam paper; 120 GeV is the neutrino-production operating point.
accelerator:fermilab-main-injector.summary_technical: 3.3 km circumference proton synchrotron, design energy 150 GeV, operated at 120 GeV for neutrino production; slip-stacked Booster batches are loaded via the Recycler. Source of the NuMI beam and of the future LBNF beam.

accelerator:fermilab-pip-ii.summary_technical: 800 MeV CW-capable superconducting RF H- linac replacing the 400 MeV normal-conducting linac, injecting into the Booster and enabling 1.2 MW of 60-120 GeV protons on the LBNF target.

accelerator:fermilab-recycler.summary_technical: 8 GeV permanent-magnet storage ring in the Main Injector tunnel (3.3 km). Built for Tevatron Run II antiproton storage, now used for Booster-batch stacking and slip stacking ahead of Main Injector acceleration.

accelerator:fermilab-tevatron.summary_technical: Superconducting proton-antiproton collider, 980 GeV per beam (1.96 TeV centre of mass in Run II, 2002-2011); collider operation from December 1985 to the September 2011 shutdown. Host of CDF and DZero.

notes: 2026-09-17: added `specs.beam_energy` (27.5 GeV, e-/e+) and `specs.proton_energy` (920 GeV) using the existing Wikipedia citation plus an independently fetched DESY-hosted page (desy.de/~ameyer/hq/node16.html, a physicist's teaching notes on the desy.de domain, treated as `secondary` rank 12 rather than `official_facility_site` since it is not DESY's own institutional page). Both agree on 27.5/920 GeV and on the 320 GeV cms energy already recorded; confidence stays `uncertain` because no source of rank <= 10 has been fetched for these two numbers specifically.

accelerator:hl-lhc.summary_technical: Luminosity upgrade of accelerator:lhc: new Nb3Sn inner triplets, crab cavities, superconducting links and collimation over ~1.2 km, targeting a factor-10 increase in integrated luminosity over the LHC design value; installed during LS3 and scheduled to begin operation in 2030.

notes: Per-ring beam energy (≈31 GeV) is recorded as a derived half of the sourced 62 GeV centre-of-mass energy; home.cern quotes only the collision energy.
accelerator:isr.summary_technical: Two interlaced proton storage rings, each 300 m in diameter, reaching 62 GeV centre-of-mass energy; first hadron collider, operated 1971-1984 and holder of the hadron-collider luminosity record until 2004.

notes: The negative hydrogen ions are converted to protons by charge-stripping foils at RCS injection (T2K instrumentation paper).
accelerator:j-parc-linac.summary_technical: 400 MeV normal-conducting H- linac (324/972 MHz RFQ, DTL, SDTL and ACS), about 300 m long, injecting into the 3 GeV RCS through charge-stripping foils.

accelerator:j-parc-main-ring.summary_technical: 30 GeV fast-extraction proton synchrotron, 1567 m circumference, design beam power ~750 kW, 760 kW reached in December 2023, with an upgrade programme towards 1.3 MW for Hyper-Kamiokande.

accelerator:j-parc-rcs.summary_technical: 3 GeV rapid-cycling synchrotron, about 350 m circumference, 25 Hz repetition, ~1 MW beam power to the Materials and Life Science Experimental Facility; injects into the main ring.

notes: No site record is created for the KEK Tsukuba campus here: site ids on the KEK campus belong to the flavour workstream.
accelerator:kek-ps.summary_technical: 12 GeV slow/fast-cycling proton synchrotron at Tsukuba, fed by a Cockcroft-Walton, a 20 MeV linac and a 500 MeV booster. Drove the K2K neutrino beamline from 1999 until the end of K2K data taking in November 2004; experiments ended in December 2005.

notes: Construction and commissioning intervals are missing: no fetched source gives KEKB construction start or first-beam dates.
The KEKB linac injector is not modelled here; it belongs to facility:kek.
accelerator:kekb.summary_technical: Asymmetric-energy e+e- double-ring collider (8 GeV HER × 3.5 GeV LER) operating on the Υ(4S) resonance, 3 km circumference; peak luminosity 2.11×10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ with crab cavities, more than 1 ab⁻¹ integrated.

notes: kind is `linac`; LANSCE's proton beam also feeds spallation-neutron and other secondary-beam facilities not modeled here.
accelerator:lansce.summary_technical: Los Alamos Neutron Science Center linac (Technical Area 53), originally LAMPF, opened June 1972; accelerates protons to 800 MeV; its beam-stop neutrinos fed the LSND experiment.

notes: Per-beam energies (≈45.5 GeV at LEP1, ≈104.5 GeV at LEP2) are recorded as derived halves of the sourced centre-of-mass energies; home.cern quotes only the collision energies.
accelerator:lep.summary_technical: 27 km e+e- storage-ring collider with four experiments (ALEPH, DELPHI, L3, OPAL). LEP1 ran at the Z pole (~91 GeV cms); after the 1995 upgrade LEP2 reached 209 GeV cms in 2000. Closed 2 November 2000; its tunnel now houses the LHC.

notes: Per-run beam energies are carried on the Interval.specs of each run (A3).
The 2012 increase from 3.5 to 4 TeV per beam is not stated on any CERN page fetched in this session; the Run 1 interval therefore records 3.5 TeV/beam with a note.
The LHC occupies the 26.7 km tunnel built for LEP (src:cern-lep-page: 'Its 27-kilometre tunnel now hosts the LHC').
accelerator:lhc.summary_technical: Superconducting proton-proton (and heavy-ion) collider of 26 659 m circumference in the former LEP tunnel; 1232 main dipoles at 1.9 K; design 7 TeV/beam (14 TeV cms) at 1e34 cm^-2 s^-1; ran at 3.5-4 TeV/beam in Run 1, 6.5 TeV/beam in Run 2 and 6.8 TeV/beam in Run 3.

accelerator:linac2.summary_technical: Proton linac delivering 50 MeV to the PS Booster from 1978 until 12 November 2018; replaced Linac1 and was itself replaced by Linac4.

accelerator:linac4.summary_technical: 86 m H- linac (RFQ to 3 MeV, DTL to 50 MeV, CCDTL to 100 MeV, PIMS to 160 MeV) injecting into the PS Booster; replaced Linac2 during the 2019-20 long shutdown.

notes: feeds_accelerator_ids records that PEP-II was injected from the SLAC linac; no source fetched in this session states this explicitly, so it is recorded as an uncited structural fact of the accelerator complex rather than a sourced claim — flag for a future agent to source or remove.
accelerator:pep-ii.summary_technical: PEP-II B-factory: an asymmetric-energy electron-positron collider at SLAC (9 GeV e- x 3.1 GeV e+, cms 10.58 GeV, tuned to the Upsilon(4S) resonance), 2.2 km circumference, feeding the BaBar detector, 1999-2008.

accelerator:ps.summary_technical: 628 m proton synchrotron, 277 room-temperature magnets (100 dipoles), top energy 26 GeV; accepts 2 GeV protons from the PS Booster or ions from LEIR and injects into the SPS.

accelerator:psb.summary_technical: Four superimposed synchrotron rings; receives 160 MeV H- from Linac4 (stripped to protons on injection) and accelerates to 2 GeV for the PS. From 1978 to 2018 it received 50 MeV protons from Linac2 and delivered 1.4 GeV.

notes: 2026-09-17 re-check: psi.ch/en/cas/hipa is reachable this session and gives an official 1.4 MW beam-power figure, correcting the prior 1.3 MW value that had been read off a different sentence in the Wikipedia article (current beam allocation to SINQ/SmuS, not the facility's own headline power). The 1974 start year is corroborated by an official PSI news story (src:facilities-verify-psi-hipa-turns-50: 'went into operation in 1974') in addition to Wikipedia.

accelerator:rhic.summary_technical: Two intersecting 3.86 km (2.4 mi) superconducting storage rings at Brookhaven National Laboratory; the world's first heavy-ion collider and only polarized-proton collider, reaching 200 GeV per colliding gold-gold nucleon pair and up to 500 GeV in polarized proton-proton collisions. Operated 2000-2026 across 25 runs; its final run ended 2026-02-06, after which the machine began conversion into the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC).

accelerator:slac-linac.summary_technical: The 3.2 km SLAC linear accelerator (operating since 1966), capable of up to 50 GeV for electrons; injector for the Stanford Linear Collider (1989-1998) and the PEP-II B-factory (1999-2008), and today for the LCLS free-electron laser (not modeled in this wave).

accelerator:slc.summary_technical: Stanford Linear Collider: SLAC's linac accelerated electrons and positrons (up to 50 GeV per beam by design) around a single-pass arc to collide at the Z resonance (~91 GeV cms, ~45.5 GeV/beam), studied by the SLD detector, 1989-1998.

notes: kind is recorded as `linac`; the SNS accelerator complex also includes an accumulator ring (not separately modeled here).
accelerator:sns.summary_technical: Spallation Neutron Source: a ~1 GeV proton linac and accumulator ring at ORNL delivering pulsed spallation neutrons from a liquid-mercury target; completed April 2006, first instruments commissioned August 2007; beam power upgraded from 1.4 MW design to 2.8 MW (Proton Power Upgrade), operating at 1.8 MW as of this session.

notes: CONFLICT on the Sp̄pS collider era: home.cern's UA1 page gives 1981-1990 ('It ran from 1981 until 1990, when the SPS was used as a proton-antiproton collider'); some literature extends the era to 1991. The sourced 1981-1990 is recorded.

accelerator:sps.summary_technical: ~7 km proton synchrotron, 1317 room-temperature magnets, top energy 450 GeV; LHC injector and fixed-target source for the North Area, NA61/SHINE, NA62, COMPASS and AWAKE; operated as the Sp̄pS proton-antiproton collider for UA1/UA2 from 1981 to 1990.

accelerator:superkekb.summary_technical: Asymmetric e+e- double-ring collider, 7 GeV HER × 4 GeV LER at √s = 10.579 GeV, 3 km circumference, using the nano-beam scheme with a large crossing angle; target luminosity 6×10³⁵ cm⁻² s⁻¹ (originally 8×10³⁵), peak achieved 5.319×10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ on 30 June 2026.

beamline:bnb.summary_technical: On-axis muon-neutrino beam from 8 GeV kinetic (8.89 GeV/c) Booster protons on a beryllium target inside a pulsed horn, mean neutrino energy about 800 MeV, serving MiniBooNE, MicroBooNE, SBND and ICARUS at baselines of order 500 m.

beamline:cngs.summary_technical: CERN Super Proton Synchrotron protons directed onto a graphite target to produce a muon-neutrino beam aimed 732 km through the Earth's crust at LNGS; operated July 2006 to December 2012, providing the neutrino source for the OPERA experiment's nu_mu -> nu_tau appearance search.

beamline:j-parc-neutrino.summary_technical: Fast-extracted 30 GeV protons from the main ring are bent 80.7 degrees towards Kamioka, hit a 91.4 cm graphite target inside three pulsed magnetic horns, and the secondary pions decay in a 96 m helium-filled volume. The resulting narrow-band muon-neutrino beam is measured at 280 m (INGRID on-axis, ND280 off-axis) and at Super-Kamiokande at 2.504 degrees off-axis.

beamline:kek-neutrino.summary_technical: Single-turn extracted 12 GeV protons from the KEK-PS onto a 66 cm long, 3 cm diameter aluminium target inside a two-horn focusing system, followed by a 200 m decay volume and a beam dump; near detectors at about 300 m, Super-Kamiokande at 250 km. Mean neutrino energy about 1.5 GeV.

beamline:lbnf.summary_technical: On-axis wide-band muon-neutrino beam from 60-120 GeV Main Injector protons, 1.0-1.2 MW initially and upgradable to 2.4 MW, with a 1285 km baseline from Fermilab to the SURF 4850 Level, together with the far-site conventional facilities.

beamline:numi.summary_technical: 120 GeV Main Injector protons on a 1 m graphite target, two magnetic horns and a 675 m decay volume, aimed 58 mrad downward toward Soudan. Served MINOS (2005-2012) and, since September 2013, NOvA (14.6 mrad off axis), MINOS+ and MINERvA.

detector:atlas.summary_technical: General-purpose 4-pi collider detector: silicon pixel + SCT + TRT inner detector in a 2 T solenoid, liquid-argon EM and forward calorimetry, scintillator-tile hadronic calorimeter, and an air-core toroid muon spectrometer. Calorimetry to |eta| = 4.9, precision tracking to |eta| < 2.5, muon measurement to |eta| < 2.7.

detector:belle-ii.summary_technical: General-purpose 4π spectrometer at the SuperKEKB interaction point: PXD, SVD, CDC, TOP and ARICH, ECL inside a 1.5 T solenoid, and the KLM in the instrumented flux return; about 1400 t, rolled in on 11 April 2017.

detector:borexino.summary_technical: Liquid-scintillator (pseudocumene+PPO) detector, 278 t active mass, ~100 t fiducial mass, in a nylon vessel with a water-Cherenkov muon veto; operated at LNGS Hall C from May 2007 to October 2021.

detector:cast.summary_technical: Straight, twin-bore prototype LHC dipole magnet (formerly LEP DELPHI cryogenics) tracking the Sun, coupled to X-ray optics and detectors for the axion helioscope technique; data-taking 2003-06-18 to 2022-12-31.

detector:cdms-ii.summary_technical: 19 Ge (~230 g) and 11 Si (~100 g) ionization-and-phonon detectors, 76 mm diameter x ~10 mm thick disks, grouped into five 6-detector towers, operated below 50 mK at Soudan.

detector:coherent-nai.summary_technical: NaIvE-185: 185 kg array of NaI[Tl] scintillator crystals installed in Neutrino Alley at the SNS in June 2016, used for charged-current neutrino interaction studies on 127-I and CEvNS background characterization ahead of a planned ton-scale expansion.

detector:comet.summary_technical: Curved-solenoid pion capture and muon transport system selecting low-momentum, negatively-charged muons off an 8 GeV, 3.2 kW J-PARC proton beam, feeding a detector solenoid instrumented for Phase-I with CyDet (cylindrical drift chamber + trigger hodoscope) and, for background studies toward Phase-II, StrECAL (straw tracker + electromagnetic calorimeter).

detector:conus-hpge-array.summary_technical: Array of four 1 kg point-contact high-purity germanium (HPGe) spectrometers with sub-300 eV ionization thresholds; operated at Brokdorf (2018-2023, 17.1 m from a 3.9 GWth reactor core) and, refurbished, at Leibstadt from November 2023 (20.7 m from a 3.6 GWth reactor core; 2.83 kg active mass from 3 of 4 detectors in the first CONUS+ analysis).

detector:cresst.summary_technical: Cryogenic transition-edge-sensor calorimeters on scintillating crystal absorbers: sapphire in CRESST-I (2000-2003), 300 g CaWO4 crystals in CRESST-II (2003-2019), and ~25 g CaWO4/Al2O3/LiAlO4 crystals in CRESST-III (from 2019) reaching nuclear-recoil thresholds of 10 eV and lower.

detector:d0.summary_technical: General-purpose collider detector, complementary to CDF, with uranium/liquid-argon calorimetry retained from Run I; upgraded for Run II (2001) with a silicon microstrip tracker, central fiber tracker, solenoidal magnet, preshower detectors, forward muon detector and forward proton detector added around the original calorimeters and muon system.

detector:damic.summary_technical: CCD array: seven 16-Mpixel CCDs (6.0 g each, ~42 g total) in the 2017-2018 SNOLAB run (11 kg-day exposure); later replaced/supplemented by two 24-Mpixel skipper CCDs for a low-energy-threshold run through at least January 2024. detector:daya-bay-antineutrino-detectors.summary_technical: Six (2011-2012) then eight (2012-2020) functionally identical Gd-doped liquid-scintillator antineutrino detectors, each ~20 t target mass, deployed across the Daya Bay near, Ling Ao near and far underground halls.

detector:donut.summary_technical: Hybrid emulsion-target (nuclear-emulsion sheets interspersed with steel/iron sheets, an emulsion-cloud-chamber-style target) followed by electronic scintillator counters and drift-chamber spectrometers, at a Tevatron fixed-target beam dump.

detector:km3net-orca.summary_technical: KM3NeT/ORCA (Oscillation Research with Cosmics in the Abyss): sea-water Cherenkov neutrino telescope at the KM3NeT-Fr site off Toulon, France (2450 m depth), designed as one building block of 115 detection units (~7 Mt instrumented seawater) for atmospheric neutrino oscillation measurements and neutrino mass ordering; 42 detection units were installed as of July 2026, with construction ongoing.

detector:mu2e.summary_technical: Production, transport and detector superconducting solenoids (25 m combined length) with a straw-tube tracker and fast CsI crystal calorimeter behind the stopping target, plus a cosmic ray veto system covering the solenoids, per the Mu2e TDR and subsequent status reports. detector:sphenix.summary_technical: sPHENIX: a 1,000 t hermetic collider detector at RHIC IP8 built around a reused 20-ton BaBar solenoid (4 K) with tungsten-scintillating-fiber electromagnetic calorimetry; construction completed April 2023, commissioned with first Au+Au data in 2023.

notes: site:bnl-rhic-ip6-star is owned by the facilities lead. It was still missing from data/atlas/sites/ when this record was first drafted (2026-09-17); the facilities lead's BNL child has since landed it, and the reference here was re-checked and resolves cleanly.
Magnet field strength not recorded this session (see experiment:star notes); technology_class 'gaseous_tpc' chosen because the TPC is described as the detector's central/defining subsystem.
detector:star.summary_technical: STAR: a 1,200 t heavy-ion collider detector at RHIC IP6, built around a 4 m diameter x 4.2 m long gaseous Time Projection Chamber inside a solenoidal magnet, providing full-azimuth charged-particle tracking within |eta| < 1.8.

notes: A detector-paper PMT count (NIM A 501, 2003) could not be extracted in this session (PDF not machine-readable by the fetch tool); the 11,129 figure is instead sourced from the official detector page, which is consistent with the 2026 INSPIRE experiment-record summary ('11,200 PMTs', an approximate paraphrase) and the SK-III restoration figure on the history page.

experiment_ids includes experiment:t2k and experiment:k2k in addition to experiment:super-kamiokande: this same physical detector serves as the far detector for both accelerator-neutrino programmes (K2K, 250 km from KEK; T2K, 295 km from J-PARC) as well as running its own solar/atmospheric/proton-decay/supernova physics programme. See src:t2k-nim-2011 ('...detected at the Super-Kamiokande...') and src:k2k-tutorial-page ('Neutrinos generated at KEK will be detected by the Super-kamiokande detector 250 km away.').
detector:super-kamiokande.summary_technical: 39.3 m diameter x 41.4 m height stainless-steel tank; inner detector of 11,129 inward-facing 20-inch PMTs (~40% photocoverage), outer veto of 1,885 8-inch PMTs; 50 kt total / 22.5 kt fiducial mass. Rebuilt/upgraded through SK-I - SK-IV after a November 2001 PMT-implosion accident (full density restored June 2006); gadolinium-loaded since August 2020 (SK-Gd).

notes: Detector total/active/fiducial mass in kg was not found on any page fetched this session; only the crystal count (24) is sourced.
Split on 2026-09-18: this record now covers only the SNOLAB payload. The earlier Soudan-era iZIP payload is now detector:supercdms-soudan (see experiment:supercdms.lineage).
detector:supercdms.summary_technical: 24-crystal Si/Ge cryogenic ionization-and-phonon payload operated at 15-30 mK at SNOLAB, succeeding an earlier-generation iZIP payload (detector:supercdms-soudan) that ran at the Soudan Underground Laboratory 2009-2015; multiple shielding layers (Cu, polyethylene, ultrapure Pb, radon barrier) suppress backgrounds.

notes: No Soudan-specific crystal count or total mass was found by any source fetched this session or the original research pass; left unsourced rather than assumed from the later SNOLAB payload's 24-crystal figure.
detector:supercdms-soudan.summary_technical: iZIP (interleaved Z-sensitive Ionization and Phonon) cryogenic Ge/Si detector payload operated at the Soudan Underground Laboratory, 2009-2015; an evolution of the CDMS-II detector design with substantially improved surface-event background rejection.

detector:telescope-array.summary_technical: Hybrid surface-detector/fluorescence-detector system: 507 scintillator counters on a 1.2 km grid over ~700 km^2, plus 38 fluorescence telescopes at three sites; extended since 2019 by TAx4 (500 further counters on a 2.08 km grid, 12 new FD telescopes, ~3000 km^2 target coverage).

notes: VERIFIER FIX (2026-09-17): status corrected 'active' -> 'shutdown' and a Long Shutdown 3 interval added (mirroring experiment:totem), because the prior record's open-ended 'operating' interval made the detector derive as permanently active even while CERN's LHC -- TOTEM's only beam source -- is in Long Shutdown 3, contradicting experiment:totem's own status.
detector:totem.summary_technical: Roman Pot silicon-strip stations (26 total) symmetric about IP5, plus T1 (CSC) and T2 (GEM) forward tracking telescopes covering pseudo-rapidity 3-7; ~3000 kg total equipment.

notes: Detector site placement carries the same LSS4-vs-LSS5 caveat as site:cern-sps-lss5-ua1 (see that record's notes): the specific SPS hall was not independently verified by a fetched source this session.
detector:ua1.summary_technical: General-purpose (4-pi) collider detector: central six-chambered imaging drift chamber (5.8 m long, 2.3 m diameter) inside an 800-tonne conventional dipole magnet, 48 lead-layer ('gondola') electromagnetic subdetectors, hadron calorimetry and muon chambers requiring about 30 km of extruded aluminium.

notes: Detector site placement carries the same LSS4-vs-LSS5 caveat as site:cern-sps-lss4-ua2 (see that record's notes): the specific SPS hall was not independently verified by a fetched source this session.

detector:ua2.summary_technical: Non-magnetic, highly segmented calorimetric spectrometer: complete electromagnetic and hadronic calorimetry down to about 5 degrees from the beam, 6,096 independent silicon dE/dx counters, no muon detector; upgraded in 1985-1987 with a scintillating-fibre tracker (and later a silicon pad detector) to improve tracking and electron identification.

notes: document_ids deliberately not written (v0.2 A1 derived field).
detector:veritas.summary_technical: Array of four 12 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes at Mount Hopkins, Arizona; full array completed January 2007, sensitive 85 GeV to >30 TeV.

detector:xenon1t.summary_technical: Dual-phase xenon TPC, 3.2 t total / 2.0 t active liquid xenon, in LNGS Hall B. Operated 2015-2018; predecessor of the XENONnT detector.

detector:xenonnt.summary_technical: Dual-phase (two-phase) xenon TPC, 8.5 t total / 5.9 t active liquid xenon, in LNGS Hall B. Upgrade of the XENON1T detector, reusing its water shield; adds a cryogenic radon-distillation column and a dedicated neutron veto.

detector:zeus.summary_technical: General-purpose ep collider detector: high-resolution compensating uranium-scintillator calorimeter, central tracking detector inside a superconducting coil, silicon micro-vertex detector, forward/backward drift-chamber and straw-tube trackers, an instrumented iron absorber for hadronic-shower tails and muon identification, and additional muon detectors covering a large solid angle.

Confidence verified rests on the passing span check against SLAC's own official figure for the length of this exact structure (not a proxy figure): the official page states the linear accelerator structure (i.e. the Klystron Gallery building measured here) is 3,073.72 m long.

End Station A (building 61) is SLAC's historic fixed-target hall where the 1969-1973 SLAC-MIT deep-inelastic-scattering experiments found the first direct evidence of quarks; it hosts the modern End Station Test Beam (ESTB) facility today. Neither ESA nor ESB corresponds to a detector/experiment entity in this atlas wave, so both are drawn only as context buildings.

The four other PEP-II interaction regions (IR-4/6/8/12) and the PEP Control Room / PEP Beam Facility (which serves the Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lab, SSRL, a separate light-source facility not modeled in HEP Atlas) have no atlas accelerator/detector/experiment entity either; drawn as context for campus completeness only.

PEP-II's circumference is officially 2,200 m (src:geo-slac-pepii-cdr-osti, the PEP-II Conceptual Design Report: 'each with a circumference of 2200 m'), but the two mapped road segments together measure only 1,320.2 m + 699.0 m = 2,019.2 m and do not close into a loop, so no `checks[]` length row is asserted here (a check against an incomplete, unclosed shape would not be a meaningful circumference measurement). See the worklog for this residual.

This ring-road proxy stands in the SLAC Research Yard around which the PEP-II (and originally PEP) storage rings ran; the five 'PEP Interaction Region' buildings (620, 640, 660, 680, 720) sit along its inferred path, of which IR-2 (620) is drawn separately as the BaBar hall.

Neutrino Alley itself is officially described as a '164-foot, or 50-meter, long hallway' in the basement of the SNS target building, with its closest point 'about 20 meters from the SNS target' (src:geo-ornl-neutrino-alley-qa), but no coordinate, OSM element or published site plan locating this corridor within the complex was found this session; see the worklog backlog.

notes: Overpass (overpass-api.de and lz4.overpass-api.de) was refusing all connections for a long stretch of this session (curl exit 7 'Failed to connect', even to /api/status) after one successful query; this matches the shared-load pattern documented in docs/atlas-worklog/GEOMETRY_cern.md. Only one South Pole query succeeded before the outage (the station node used for geometry:south-pole-station-marker); a follow-up unrestricted building/man_made query and a search for the IceCube Laboratory (ICL) building did not complete this session. See the worklog for the retry outcome.

The 86-string IceCube in-ice array, IceTop, DeepCore, the ARA stations, AMANDA, the IceCube Upgrade and IceCube-Gen2 are all deliberately left unlocated: IceCube's own coordinate system is a local South Pole grid (Northings/Eastings) documented on docs.icecube.aq, which returned HTTP 401 Unauthorized to every fetch attempt this session and so could not be read or quoted; no other fetched source states how that grid's axes relate to true geographic north. Nothing in this record is derived from that unreachable page.

notes: The array is described as growing annually (12 clusters implied by 96 strings / 8 strings-per-cluster as of the winter 2023 season cited here; web search indicates further growth to 14-15 clusters by 2024-2025, but that could not be independently fetched and quoted this session, so only the 2023 status paper's own directly-quoted numbers are used in the data records). Only one representative cluster's footprint is drawn (geometry:baikal-gvd-cluster-footprint); the full multi-cluster array footprint is not stated by any source fetched this session and is not derived here (drawing a hexagonal-packing guess for 12+ clusters at 300 m spacing would assume a specific packing shape that is not itself sourced).

The onshore 'shore station' housing the control/DAQ systems is mentioned in secondary sources (~4 km from the lake site, near the Ivanovka river outfall) but no source fetched this session gives it a citable building-level position, and Overpass access was unreachable for most of this session (see map:amundsen-scott-south-pole-station's notes) so no OSM search for it could be completed. Left as a backlog item rather than drawn or guessed.
map:baikal-deep-underwater-neutrino-tele.summary_technical: Local map for facility:baikal-deep-underwater-neutrino-telescope. One surveyed point (the collaboration's own published 51 46'N 104 24'E) and one derived ~120 m-diameter circle for a single cluster's string layout (per the 2023 status paper, arXiv:2309.16310); the full multi-cluster array footprint is not sourced and not drawn.

notes: This map is honestly thin: the surface administrative building and the Neutrino settlement are drawn from OpenStreetMap, but the tunnels themselves and the SAGE underground hall are not, because no fetched source this session gives the tunnel's path/bearing and OpenStreetMap does not appear to trace it (no way was found via Nominatim name search for 'Baksan tunnel' or Cyrillic equivalents, and a bounding-box tag search that Overpass would have allowed was not possible — Overpass was unreachable throughout this session, see the facility worklog).

SAGE's own 1999 paper (src:sage-1999-capture-rate) states the laboratory is '3.5 km from the entrance of a horizontal adit excavated into the side of Mount Andyrchi' with a 60x10x12 m chamber (src:geo-euro-ug-pandola-2011); this is recorded here and in the facility worklog as backlog for a future pass with Overpass access or a topographic source giving the tunnel's bearing.

Area', drawn here as geometry:bnl-ags-experimental-area-building) is flagged in the worklog as a lead for whoever creates that site record.

map:canfranc-underground-laboratory.summary_technical: One local map for facility:canfranc-underground-laboratory. map:cern.summary_technical: One local map for facility:cern spanning the Meyrin and Prévessin sites and the full LHC/LEP tunnel footprint. map:chooz.summary_technical: Reactor-building footprints from OpenStreetMap; no laboratory position drawn because two cores alone leave a mirror ambiguity.

map:cjpl.summary_technical: Local map for facility:cjpl. notes: Facility status is 'construction'; individual telescope positions are planned, not yet built/surveyed, per CTAO's own site description.
map:ctao-south-paranal.summary_technical: One local map for facility:ctao-south-paranal. notes: The three halls are drawn as derived points (not footprints): their positions come from multilateration, not from a survey or a tracing; accuracy_m on each hall covers the fit residual and the use of reactor-building centroids as proxies for the core centres.
map:daya-bay-reactor-neutrino-lab.summary_technical: Reactor-building footprints from OpenStreetMap (georeferenced); EH1–EH3 positions derived by least-squares multilateration from the six cores using the AD-to-core baselines of arXiv:1508.03943 Table 2 (survey uncertainty < 18 mm); overburdens from §2.2/Table 1 of the same paper.

map:desy.summary_technical: One local map for facility:desy spanning the Hamburg-Bahrenfeld campus and the full HERA ring footprint. Geometry sourced from OpenStreetMap (way 24973326 for the HERA ring; way 276641657 for the campus boundary; way 131496014 for the North Hall/H1 building; way 297515305 for the PETRA III storage-ring tunnel, drawn as context) cross-checked against DESY's own published HERA ring length and depth figures.

map:fermilab.summary_technical: Local to-scale map of the Fermilab Batavia campus: a derived circle for the Booster ring (474 m sourced circumference, OSM-fit centre) and for the Tevatron ring (6.3 km sourced circumference, OSM ring-road-fit centre, cross-checked against the OSM-sourced CDF and D0 hall positions); georeferenced/derived OSM building footprints for the CDF Hall, D0 Assembly Building, MINOS and NOvA near-detector surface buildings, MiniBooNE Detector Building, the LArTF/MicroBooNE hall, a positionally-identified ICARUS-T600 hall and the Muon g-2 MC-1 building; derived target_station/beamline features for BNB and NuMI, each anchored on two independently-named OSM footprints rather than a coarse site point, with passing distance/azimuth checks; an approximate linac axis; context-only campus boundary, Main Injector-area grassland and MC-2 polygons; and inferred-direction lines for the NuMI and LBNF beams, now starting from the derived NuMI target. The Main Injector, Recycler, PIP-II, KTeV, Mu2e, SeaQuest/NM4, SBND (candidate footprints found but not confidently identified), MINERvA, DONUT, SENSEI, DAMIC (prototype) and the DUNE near detector are unlocated, each with a sourced reason and backlog.

map:kamioka-observatory.summary_technical: Local map for facility:kamioka-observatory spanning the Mozumi mine (site:kamioka-mozumi-mine-super-kamiokande, site:kamioka-kamland) and the Tochibora mine (site:kamioka-hyper-kamiokande-tochibora), 8 km apart. map:kek.summary_technical: One local map for facility:kek covering the Tsukuba campus: the 3016 m KEKB/SuperKEKB ring tunnel (OSM way 138322704, cross-checked against the SuperKEKB accelerator paper's own machine-parameter table), the Tsukuba interaction hall (Belle, Belle II) and the ring's Oho/Fuji/Nikko straight-section halls, the KEK injector linac building, a building tentatively identified with the historic KEK-PS North Counter Hall, and an inferred-direction line for the K2K beam toward Super-Kamiokande.

notes: Portopalo di Capo Passero, the nearest shore town, is ~100 km from this site (per the KM3NeT-It page and the Letter of Intent) -- more than the 60 km limit for drawing a shore feature as context on the same map (and more than the validator's own 60 km hard error on feature position). It is not drawn here and there is no separate facility/site record for it to anchor a linked map either; noted in the worklog as a backlog item only.

Overpass access was unreachable for most of this session (see map:amundsen-scott-south-pole-station's notes); a sea site has no OSM features to fetch in any case, per the research brief, so this did not block this map.
map:km3net-arca.summary_technical: Local map for the KM3NeT-It / ARCA deep-sea site (facility:km3net). One surveyed point (the collaboration's own published 36°16' N 16°06' E) and one derived ~1 km-diameter circle for a single ARCA building block (R=500 m per the KM3NeT 2.0 Letter of Intent). ARCA and ORCA are ~900 km apart and cannot share a to-scale map; see map:km3net-orca (linked).

notes: ANTARES (site:antares-toulon, detector:antares) sits about 10 km east of this site per the Letter of Intent ('ORCA ... approximately 10 kilometers west of the existing ANTARES telescope site'), but site:antares-toulon carries facility_id: null -- it does not belong to any atlas facility, so per this workstream's scope it is out of map:km3net-orca's inventory (not drawn, and not listed in unlocated[] either, since unlocated[] is for this facility's own entities). Its own coordinate is separately only 'approximate' with precision_m 12000 (a corroborated estimate, not a directly published lat/lon), which is too coarse to add a defensibly-placed context point here anyway. Left as a backlog item in the worklog rather than drawn.

The ORCA shore control station has moved between buildings during this session's research window (Institut Michel Pacha, La Seyne-sur-Mer originally; the Brégaillon/Ifremer site since January 2024; the MEUST building once ready), so no single building was confidently identified as 'the' current shore station to draw as OSM context this session; Overpass access was also unreachable for most of this session (see map:amundsen-scott-south-pole-station's notes). Left as a backlog item.
Overpass had no bearing on the two drawn features here (a sea site has no OSM footprint, per the research brief).
map:km3net-orca.summary_technical: Local map for the KM3NeT-Fr / ORCA deep-sea site (facility:km3net). One surveyed point (the collaboration's own published 42°48' N 06°02' E) and one derived ~200 m-diameter circle for the single ORCA building block, its radius estimated by scaling ARCA's sourced R=500 m by the two blocks' relative string spacing (both from the KM3NeT 2.0 Letter of Intent). ARCA and ORCA are ~900 km apart and cannot share a to-scale map; see map:km3net-arca (linked).

map:leibstadt-nuclear-power-plant.summary_technical: Reactor-building footprint from OpenStreetMap (georeferenced); CONUS+ drawn as a derived point at the building centroid with widened accuracy for the unresolved offset.

map:lhaaso-daocheng.summary_technical: One local map for facility:lhaaso-daocheng. notes: Linked map: map:cern, because beamline:cngs (CERN's own beamline, facility_id facility:cern) names site:lngs-hall-c as its far_detector_site_ids target (732 km baseline, 2006-2012 beam operation for OPERA/ICARUS). geometry:lngs-hall-a, geometry:lngs-hall-b and geometry:lngs-hall-c intentionally share one derived coordinate (the midpoint of the sourced ~700 m access-zone stretch): no source fetched this session distinguishes the three halls' order or position within that zone. This will raise the validator's geometry-duplicate-shape warning for all three pairs; documented here and in the facility worklog per the contract's 'a warning you leave must be explained' rule, and not avoided by leaving any of the three sites unlocated, since a sourced (if coarse) position is available for all three and is more informative than omission.

The Pandola 2011 overview (src:geo-euro-ug-pandola-2011) names several LNGS experiments not present in this atlas dataset (Gator, MACRO, WArP, LUNA, COBRA, DAMA/Libra, STELLA/GEMPI2); they are not listed in unlocated[] because they are not atlas entities this session may create (out of this geometry-research brief's scope) — flagged in the facility worklog as backlog for whichever lead owns LNGS's experiment roster.
map:lngs.summary_technical: One local map for facility:lngs. The A24 Gran Sasso road tunnel (OSM relation 9617984) is drawn as context; the underground laboratory's own position is derived from the official emergency plan's motorway chainage of its entrance/exit doors (km 124.150/123.440 against the tunnel's own km 117.653-127.829), giving a ~700 m sourced zone about 5.8-6.5 km from the Assergi portal. Halls A, B and C are drawn at that zone's midpoint, undifferentiated. The surface External Laboratories / Centro Direzionale complex at Assergi carries both an OSM building footprint and the emergency plan's own surveyed WGS84 coordinate (79.6 m apart, corroborating each other).

notes: Overpass (overpass-api.de and lz4.overpass-api.de) refused essentially every connection attempt for LANL/ORNL after the SLAC extract succeeded (TCP connection refused, then HTTP 429, then connection refused again); overpass.kumi.systems and overpass.osm.ch both answered but returned zero elements even for known-good queries and were dropped as likely partial/regional mirrors. maps.mail.ru/osm/tools/overpass/api/interpreter, suggested mid-session, did return real, complete data: a 1,817-element extract of the wider Los Alamos townsite (streets, apartments, generic industrial buildings, none named or tagged in any way suggesting LANSCE), and a tight 700 m box directly around the LANSCE node itself came back with zero building ways. TA-53's accelerator/experimental core is therefore genuinely almost unmapped in OpenStreetMap, not merely unreached this session. Nominatim's /search and /lookup endpoints were reachable throughout and are the source of the one point drawn on this map.

TA-53 is a security-sensitive area of Los Alamos National Laboratory: per the research brief, only accelerator/experimental areas shown on public LANSCE maps may be depicted, never fences or gates. No fence, gate or access-control feature is drawn or was found.
map:los-alamos-national-laboratory.summary_technical: One local map for facility:los-alamos-national-laboratory. Only OpenStreetMap node 8041862150 ('LANSCE') was locatable this session; the 800 m side-coupled-cavity linac (accelerator:lansce) and the LSND detector's position are both unlocated, for lack of a public, sufficiently precise source.

notes: The pre-existing site:lsm-frejus coordinate (45.1962509, 6.6667021, precision_m 500, src:lsm-osm-nominatim) is an OSM/Nominatim point essentially co-located with the Carré Science surface outreach building (geometry:modane-carre-sciences-point), about 6.4 km from the underground laboratory itself by tunnel. See the facility worklog for a proposed correction using geometry:modane-lsm-underground's own coordinate.

The Fréjus road tunnel gained a second, parallel tube in July 2025 (src:geo-modane-sftrf-second-tube-pr); geometry:modane-tunnel-frejus's representation is kept 'approximate' because this session could not confirm from OSM tags alone which of the two tubes its traced line follows over its full length (Overpass, which would have let this be resolved by relation membership, was unreachable). Both tubes run closely parallel and are the same length, so the practical effect on the laboratory's derived position is small.
map:modane-underground-laboratory.summary_technical: One local map for facility:modane-underground-laboratory. The Fréjus road tunnel (OSM ways 101986702 + 317397424) is drawn as context; the laboratory itself is OSM's own tagged area (way 235115147, addr:housename 'PK 6.5, Tunnel du Fréjus'), independently corroborated by this session's own geometric midpoint of the tunnel line (148 m apart) and by a 2009 CNRS Images caption describing the access point as exactly at the tunnel's centre.

notes: Overpass (overpass-api.de and lz4.overpass-api.de) refused essentially every connection attempt for LANL/ORNL after the SLAC extract succeeded (TCP connection refused, then HTTP 429, then connection refused again); overpass.kumi.systems accepted queries but appears to serve only a partial/regional dataset (zero elements even for a query overpass-api.de had already answered for the same SLAC bbox) and was not trusted; overpass.osm.ch answered but likewise returned zero elements for known-good queries and was dropped for the same reason. maps.mail.ru/osm/tools/overpass/api/interpreter, suggested mid-session, did return real data (25 buildings inside the SNS complex boundary, see the unlocated row below and the worklog) but timed out (HTTP 504) on anything larger than a single 'building' filter over a sub-1 km box, so the ring/linac search itself could not complete. Nominatim's /search and /lookup endpoints (a separate, lighter-weight OSM service) were reachable throughout and are the source of the complex boundary drawn on this map.

COHERENT's four operating sub-detectors (CENNS-10, CsI, Ge, NaI) all sit in Neutrino Alley, officially 'about 20 meters from the SNS target' at its closest point and 50 m long overall (src:geo-ornl-neutrino-alley-qa); none is drawn individually, since no source this session gives any one detector's position along the alley or a coordinate/heading for the alley itself, only its overall length and closest-approach distance. See the worklog.
map:oak-ridge-national-laboratory.summary_technical: One local map for facility:oak-ridge-national-laboratory. notes: map-center-far warning is expected and accepted: the map centre is the array's own geometric centroid (~40 km from site:malargue-auger, which is the Observatory's administrative HQ address in the town of Malargüe, not the array's centre -- that site record already documents this distinction).

The four fluorescence-detector buildings (Los Leones, Los Morados, Loma Amarilla, Coihueco) are not drawn: despite many fetch attempts (arXiv 1502.01323, 0907.4282, 1011.6523 via WebFetch and an r.jina.ai text-extraction proxy; the Auger Open Data portal; several web searches), no coordinate for any individual FD site could be seen verbatim in a fetched source this session, and Overpass (which might have found them as named OSM buildings) refused every connection attempt. See worklog backlog.

geometry:auger-sd750-infill-boundary's computed area (29.3 km^2) does not closely match the collaboration's own quoted '23.5 km^2, 61-detector' infill figure; no checks[] row is asserted for it (see that record's own note).
map:pierre-auger-observatory.summary_technical: One local map for facility:pierre-auger-observatory. The main (1500 m spacing) and infill (750 m spacing) surface-detector array boundaries are convex hulls computed this session from the 1690-row station position table in the Observatory's own public Open Data release (sdMap.csv, Zenodo record 10488964), UTM zone 19S converted to WGS84. The four fluorescence-detector buildings (Los Leones, Los Morados, Loma Amarilla, Coihueco) could not be individually located this session (see notes) and are not drawn.

notes: Overpass (overpass-api.de and lz4.overpass-api.de) refused every connection attempt for the entire PSI/KIT portion of this session (curl: 'Failed to connect ... Couldn't connect to server', not a 429/504 that a backoff would clear). The campus boundary was recovered through Nominatim's polygon_geojson=1 output instead (same underlying OSM way data), but Nominatim only supports name search, not Overpass's tag/bbox queries -- so the HIPA ring-cyclotron building and the large experimental hall (housing MEG-II and Mu3e in the piE5 area) could not be located by name and are not drawn. Named locality nodes 'PSI West' (47.5368N, 8.2222E) and 'PSI Ost' (47.5386N, 8.2300E) corroborate which OSM polygon is which bank, but are themselves place labels, not building footprints, so they are not drawn either.

map:psi.summary_technical: One local map for facility:psi. map:roque-de-los-muchachos-observatory.summary_technical: One local map for facility:roque-de-los-muchachos-observatory, shared by experiment:magic and experiment:ctao (CTAO-North). map:sierra-negra.summary_technical: One local map for facility:sierra-negra. Drawn as a single reference point at the array's own published coordinate (18.99N, 97.31W), tighter than the existing site record's Nominatim peak-geocode point; the 300-tank footprint has no sourced overall outline shape this session.

notes: geometry:slac-collider-experimental-hall-sld and geometry:slac-collider-experimental-hall-dmradio are drawn over the SAME OpenStreetMap polygon (way 232494549, Building 750): the SLD detector occupied this hall 1991-1998, and the DMRadio-m3 axion search is independently sourced (src:geo-slac-dmradio-prd-2022) to occupy the same building today. This is an intentional geometry-duplicate-shape pair, not an error: two different, independently sourced entities in the same physical hall at different times.

PEP-II's ring is drawn only partially (geometry:slac-pep-ii-partial-ring): the two 'PEP Ring Road' ways found in OpenStreetMap do not close into a loop and together cover only about 2,019 m of the collider's official 2,200 m circumference (src:geo-slac-pepii-cdr-osti), so no ring length check is asserted. See the worklog for the residual and backlog.

Overpass (overpass-api.de / lz4.overpass-api.de) accepted one extract for this campus and then refused further connections for the remainder of the session (HTTP 429, then outright TCP connection refusals); a lower-load alternate mirror was tried but returned zero results even for a query that overpass-api.de had already answered, so it was not used further. All SLAC geometry in this map comes from that single extract plus the sources cited above.
map:slac.summary_technical: One local map for facility:slac. Geometry sourced from a single OpenStreetMap Overpass extract (the SLAC property boundary way 634083231; the Klystron Gallery building way 162058026, checked against SLAC's own '3,073.72 m' figure for that structure; the two 'PEP Ring Road' ways; the PEP Interaction Region 2 / BaBar hall and Collider Experimental Hall / SLD-DMRadio-m3 hall buildings; and nine other campus buildings drawn as context), cross-referenced against the official SLAC Area Map building-number table and the PEP-II Conceptual Design Report's circumference figure.

map:snolab.summary_technical: Local map for facility:snolab. Surface geometry from OpenStreetMap (the SNOLAB office node and the Creighton Mine industrial landuse polygon). The underground cavity is a derived 22 m circle centred on the SNO NIM detector paper's own published coordinate, cross-checked against the same paper's stated diameter. SNOLAB's other experiment halls (SNO+, DEAP-3600, DAMIC, SuperCDMS SNOLAB, nEXO, NEWS-G) share this one sourced site coordinate and have no distinct footprint located this session.

map:soudan-underground-laboratory.summary_technical: Local map for facility:soudan-underground-laboratory. Surface geometry is the NRHP-listed Soudan Mine shaft house from OpenStreetMap. The Level 27 laboratory is drawn as a surveyed point taken directly from the MINOS Collaboration's own published coordinate (PRD 76, 052003), reused verbatim from site:soudan-minos-far-detector; MINOS far detector, CDMS II and SuperCDMS Soudan all share this one position, having no independently sourced distinct footprint.

map:surf.summary_technical: Local map for facility:surf spanning the Lead, SD surface campus (OSM building footprints for the Yates and Ross shaft head-frames and hoists) and the 4850 Level (1478 m depth). The Davis Campus cavern (LZ, Majorana Demonstrator) is drawn from its own surveyed coordinate (SURF Physics Procedia Table 5); the LBNF/DUNE far-detector caverns on the same level remain unlocated for lack of a sourced offset from the Ross Shaft.

The 507-station 1.2 km SD grid and the three fluorescence-detector sites (Black Rock Mesa, Long Ridge, Middle Drum) are not drawn: their widely repeated coordinates trace only to a hobbyist astronomy site (cleardarksky.com, also Wikipedia's own citation), not to an official TA page or paper fetched this session (telescopearray.org and known mirrors were unreachable). See worklog backlog.
map:telescope-array-utah.summary_technical: One local map for facility:telescope-array-utah. Drawn as a single reference point at the array's own published centre (39.3N, 112.9W), tighter than the existing site record's Delta-Utah town geocode; extent_m set large (20 km) to reflect the array's true ~700 km2 scale even though only the centre point is drawn this session.

EXO-200's own underground position within the North Experimental Area is not sourced this session beyond its 655 m depth, so nothing is drawn on that level.

notes: The near hall's distance checks to units 3–6 sit 3–4 % from the TDR figures (10–28 m), consistent with using reactor-building centroids as proxies for core centres over 300–740 m baselines; the tolerance on those checks is widened to 5 % with that reason and accuracy_m raised accordingly — see the geometry record.
map:yonggwang-hanbit-reactor-site.summary_technical: Reactor-unit footprints and plant boundary from OpenStreetMap; near/far hall positions derived by multilateration from the six units using Table 1.2 of the RENO TDR (arXiv:1003.1391); the assignment of reactor numbers to buildings is the only one of the 720 permutations that fits.

claim.quote: An improved value for the lifetime of the (anti-)hypertriton has been obtained using the data sample of Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 5.02 TeV collected by the ALICE experiment at the LHC.

notes: This is an ALICE-specific hypertriton lifetime measurement; a separate, unrelated STAR-experiment hypertriton mass-difference/CPT paper (also on arXiv, coincidentally an adjacent id) was found during research and explicitly excluded from this record after its full text showed it used STAR detector data, not ALICE.
result:alice-hypertriton-lifetime-2019.summary_technical: ALICE measurement of the (anti-)hypertriton lifetime via its two-body mesonic decay channel in Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 5.02 TeV: tau = 242(+34/-38 stat) +/- 17(syst) ps, compatible with available theoretical predictions and contributing to resolving the hypertriton lifetime puzzle.
result:alice-hypertriton-lifetime-2019.why_it_matters: The hypertriton (a proton, neutron and Lambda hyperon bound together) is the lightest known hypernucleus; its lifetime, if much shorter than a free Lambda's, would point to unexpectedly strong hyperon-nucleon interactions relevant to the physics of neutron-star interiors. This measurement addresses a long-standing discrepancy between earlier, scattered lifetime measurements (the 'hypertriton lifetime puzzle').

claim.quote: A suppression of the inclusive J/psi yield in Pb-Pb is observed with respect to the one measured in pp collisions scaled by the number of binary nucleon-nucleon collisions.

notes: result_type is 'measurement' rather than 'observation': although the abstract's passive wording ('is observed') would satisfy A16's keyword check for 'observation', J/psi suppression itself was already established at SPS/RHIC energies before ALICE; this paper measures the effect at LHC energy, so 'measurement' better matches the collaboration's own framing (a suppression factor with quoted uncertainties) and avoids over-classifying a measurement as a first observation.
result:alice-jpsi-suppression-pbpb-2012.summary_technical: ALICE measurement of inclusive J/psi production at forward rapidity (2.5 < y < 4) in Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 2.76 TeV: nuclear modification factor R_AA = 0.545 +/- 0.032 (stat) +/- 0.083 (syst), 0-80% centrality, flat in centrality and significantly less suppressed than at SPS/RHIC energies, consistent with a charmonium-regeneration component from deconfined charm quarks.
result:alice-jpsi-suppression-pbpb-2012.why_it_matters: Charmonium (J/psi) suppression was proposed as a signature of quark-gluon plasma formation via colour screening; measuring it at LHC energy, and finding less suppression than at lower-energy machines, tests whether charm quarks recombine into new J/psi mesons inside the plasma.

claim.quote: Here we present the first observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions.

result:alice-strangeness-enhancement-pp-.summary_technical: ALICE measurement (pp at sqrt(s) = 7 TeV) of multi-strange hadron (K0s, Lambda, Xi, Omega) yields relative to pions as a function of charged-particle multiplicity: first observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions, with yields at the highest multiplicities comparable to those in Pb-Pb collisions.
result:alice-strangeness-enhancement-pp-.why_it_matters: Strangeness enhancement was long considered a signature of quark-gluon plasma formation in heavy-ion collisions specifically; finding it in ordinary proton-proton collisions at high multiplicity blurs the line between 'small' and 'large' collision systems and challenges the idea that QGP-like behaviour requires heavy nuclei.

claim.quote: which yields an observed (expected) significance of 5.4 (5.5) standard deviations, thus providing direct observation of the Higgs boson decay into b-quarks.

result:atlas-hbb-observation-2018.summary_technical: VH production, H -> bb, using 79.8 fb^-1 of 13 TeV data combined with 7 and 8 TeV results: observed (expected) significance 5.4 (5.5) standard deviations.
result:atlas-hbb-observation-2018.why_it_matters: H -> bb is the dominant Higgs decay mode; observing it at the predicted rate confirmed the Standard Model coupling of the Higgs boson to down-type quarks.

claim.quote: This observation, which has a significance of 5.9 standard deviations, corresponding to a background fluctuation probability of 1.7x10^-9, is compatible with the production and decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson.

notes: Collaboration wording is "observation of a new particle", not "discovery of the Higgs boson"; the identification with the Standard Model Higgs boson was established by later analyses (see result:atlas-nature-higgs-2022).
ATLAS announced the result publicly on 4 July 2012; the cited arXiv preprint was submitted 31 July 2012 and published as Phys. Lett. B 716 (2012) 1.
result:atlas-higgs-observation-2012.summary_technical: Combined search in the gamma-gamma, ZZ* and WW* channels using up to 4.8 fb^-1 at 7 TeV and 5.8 fb^-1 at 8 TeV: local significance 5.9 sigma at m = 126.0 +/- 0.4 (stat.) +/- 0.4 (sys.) GeV, compatible with the Standard Model Higgs boson.
result:atlas-higgs-observation-2012.why_it_matters: This was the observation that completed the Standard Model's particle content, announced jointly with CMS on 4 July 2012 and the starting point of a decade of precision Higgs measurements.

claim.quote: the observed (expected) significance amounts to 6.4 (5.4) standard deviations and constitutes an observation of H->tautau decays.

result:atlas-htautau-observation-2018.summary_technical: Combination of boosted-Higgs and VBF categories using 13 TeV data (36.1 fb^-1): observed (expected) significance 6.4 (5.4) standard deviations for H -> tau tau, an ATLAS-only observation.
result:atlas-htautau-observation-2018.why_it_matters: It was ATLAS's own first observation of the Higgs boson coupling directly to leptons, testing the Yukawa-coupling structure of the Standard Model in a second fermion channel after b quarks and top quarks.

claim.quote: This letter describes the observation of the light-by-light scattering process, gamma gamma -> gamma gamma, in Pb+Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 5.02 TeV.

result:atlas-lbyl-observation-2019.summary_technical: Ultraperipheral Pb+Pb collisions at 5.02 TeV per nucleon pair, 1.73 nb^-1 (Nov 2018): 59 gamma-gamma -> gamma-gamma candidates against a background of 12 +/- 3 events, 8.2 sigma significance, fiducial cross section 78 +/- 13 (stat.) +/- 7 (syst.) +/- 3 (lumi.) nb.
result:atlas-lbyl-observation-2019.why_it_matters: Light-by-light scattering is forbidden in classical electrodynamics and occurs only through virtual charged-particle loops in QED; observing it directly tests the Standard Model in an extreme low-background regime and constrains new light, weakly-charged particles.

claim.quote: These tests reveal that the Higgs boson discovered ten years ago is remarkably consistent with the predictions of the theory and provide stringent constraints on many models of new phenomena beyond the Standard Model.

result:atlas-nature-higgs-2022.summary_technical: Combination of ATLAS Run 1 and Run 2 (up to 139 fb^-1 at 13 TeV) Higgs measurements: production and decay signal strengths across the main channels, mass and width constraints, and searches for beyond-Standard-Model couplings, published in Nature 607 (2022) 52.
result:atlas-nature-higgs-2022.why_it_matters: It is ATLAS's most complete single-experiment statement of the Higgs boson's properties, the benchmark that HL-LHC precision measurements will be compared against.

claim.quote: An exclusion limit at the 95% confidence level on the mass of the gluino is set at 2.30 TeV for a simplified model containing only a gluino and the lightest neutralino, assuming the latter is massless.

result:atlas-squark-gluino-limit-2020.summary_technical: Search for squarks and gluinos in jets + missing transverse momentum final states using the full Run 2 dataset (139 fb^-1 at 13 TeV): no significant excess observed; 95% CL exclusion of gluino masses up to 2.30 TeV in a simplified model with a massless lightest neutralino, extending earlier limits.
result:atlas-squark-gluino-limit-2020.why_it_matters: This is ATLAS's most stringent Run 2 exclusion of a leading class of supersymmetric partner particles, a landmark limit that shapes the remaining parameter space searched at the HL-LHC.

claim.quote: The mass of the top quark is measured to be m_top = 172.08 +/- 0.39 (stat) +/- 0.82 (syst) GeV.

result:atlas-topmass-measurement-2018.summary_technical: Lepton+jets ttbar candidates from 20.2 fb^-1 of 8 TeV data, template method: m_top = 172.08 +/- 0.39 (stat.) +/- 0.82 (syst.) GeV, combined with previous ATLAS results.
result:atlas-topmass-measurement-2018.why_it_matters: The top-quark mass enters the electroweak fit and the calculation of the stability of the Higgs potential, so sharper top-mass measurements sharpen Standard Model consistency tests.

claim.quote: the observed significance is 5.8 standard deviations, compared to an expectation of 4.9 standard deviations.

result:atlas-tth-observation-2018.summary_technical: Combination of ttH searches in multilepton, bb and diphoton final states at 7, 8 and 13 TeV (up to 79.8 fb^-1 at 13 TeV): 5.8 sigma observed, 4.9 sigma expected.
result:atlas-tth-observation-2018.why_it_matters: The top-Higgs Yukawa coupling is the largest in the Standard Model; a direct ttH observation confirmed it at (within uncertainties) the predicted strength rather than through loop-level processes alone.

claim.quote: yielding m_W = 80370 +/- 7 (stat.) +/- 11 (exp. syst.) +/- 14 (mod. syst.) MeV = 80370 +/- 19 MeV

result:atlas-wmass-measurement-2017.summary_technical: W -> lepton nu candidates from 4.6 fb^-1 of 7 TeV data, template fits to lepton transverse momentum and transverse mass: m_W = 80370 +/- 19 MeV, combining statistical, experimental-systematic and modelling uncertainties.
result:atlas-wmass-measurement-2017.why_it_matters: The W-boson mass is tightly linked by the Standard Model to the top-quark and Higgs-boson masses; a precise measurement is a stringent test of the electroweak sector and a probe for physics beyond the Standard Model.

claim.quote: Evidence of the Purely Leptonic Decay B- --> tau- nu_tau-bar

notes: The collaboration's word for this result is 'evidence' (in the title); it is not recorded as an observation.
result:belle-b-to-tau-nu-evidence-2006.summary_technical: First evidence for B⁻ → τ⁻ ν̅_τ in 414 fb⁻¹ at the Υ(4S) with 3.5σ significance, B = (1.79 ⁺⁰·⁵⁶₋₀.₄₉(stat) ⁺⁰·⁴⁶₋₀.₅₁(syst)) × 10⁻⁴, giving the first direct determination of the B decay constant f_B.
result:belle-b-to-tau-nu-evidence-2006.why_it_matters: A tree-level, helicity-suppressed decay sensitive to charged-Higgs exchange; the first direct measurement of f_B|V_ub|.

claim.quote: Observation of Large CP Violation in the Neutral B Meson System

notes: Companion measurement to BaBar's contemporaneous result; that is not recorded here.
result:belle-cp-violation-observation-20.summary_technical: Time-dependent measurement of CP asymmetry in B⁰ → (cc̅)K⁰ and related modes at the Υ(4S), giving sin 2φ₁ = 0.99 ± 0.14(stat) ± 0.06(syst) and excluding the CP-conserving hypothesis.
result:belle-cp-violation-observation-20.why_it_matters: Established CP violation in the B system and validated the Kobayashi-Maskawa mechanism as the dominant source of CP violation in quark flavour transitions.

claim.quote: Evidence for $D^0 - \bar{D}^0$ Mixing

result:belle-d0-mixing-evidence-2007.summary_technical: Measurement of y_CP = (1.31 ± 0.32(stat) ± 0.25(syst))% from lifetime differences between CP-eigenstate and flavour-eigenstate D⁰ decays in 540 fb⁻¹, 3.2σ from zero, with no evidence for CP violation.
result:belle-d0-mixing-evidence-2007.why_it_matters: Completed the picture of neutral-meson mixing: mixing is now established in the K, B, B_s and D systems, and charm mixing is a sensitive probe of new physics in the up-quark sector.

claim.quote: we determine the branching fraction of the decay $B^{+}\rightarrow K^{+}\nu\bar{\nu}$ to be $[2.3 \pm 0.5(\mathrm{stat})^{+0.5}_{-0.4}(\mathrm{syst})]\times 10^{-5}$, providing the first evidence for this decay at $3.5$ standard deviations.

notes: The collaboration's own word is 'evidence'; the paper is not described as an observation.
result:belle-ii-b-to-k-nunu-evidence-202.summary_technical: Inclusive-tag and hadronic-tag searches in 362 fb⁻¹ at the Υ(4S) combine to B(B⁺ → K⁺ νν̅) = [2.3 ± 0.5(stat) ⁺⁰·⁵₋₀.₄(syst)] × 10⁻⁵, the first evidence for the decay at 3.5σ and 2.7σ above the Standard Model expectation.
result:belle-ii-b-to-k-nunu-evidence-202.why_it_matters: A flavour-changing neutral current with a clean theoretical prediction; the mild excess over the Standard Model has become one of the most watched flavour anomalies.

claim.quote: we measure the $τ$ mass to be $1777.09 ± 0.08 ± 0.11 \,\mathrm{MeV\!/c^2}$, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic. This result is the most precise to date.

notes: Journal publication was not confirmed on a source fetched in this session.
result:belle-ii-tau-mass-measurement-202.summary_technical: Pseudomass-endpoint measurement in τ⁻ → π⁻π⁺π⁻ ν_τ using ~175 million e⁺e⁻ → τ⁺τ⁻ events in 190 fb⁻¹ at √s = 10.579 GeV, giving m_τ = 1777.09 ± 0.08(stat) ± 0.11(syst) MeV/c².
result:belle-ii-tau-mass-measurement-202.why_it_matters: The tau mass enters tests of lepton universality and of the Standard Model's lepton sector; this measurement was the most precise at the time of publication.

claim.quote: We present a determination of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix element |Vcb| from the decay B to D l nu_l using a 365 fb^-1 e+e- to Upsilon(4S) to B Bbar data sample recorded by the Belle II experiment at the SuperKEKB collider.

result:belle-ii-vcb-measurement-2025.summary_technical: Inclusive-tag determination of |Vcb| from B0->D-(->K+pi-pi-) l+ nu_l and B+->D0bar(->K+pi-) l+ nu_l decays in 365 fb^-1 of Belle II Upsilon(4S) data, using the recoil variable w=v_B.v_D and lattice-QCD form-factor averages. Reports B(B0->D- l+ nu_l) = (2.06 +/- 0.05stat +/- 0.10sys)%, B(B+->D0bar l+ nu_l) = (2.31 +/- 0.04stat +/- 0.09sys)%, a lepton-flavor-universality ratio B(B->D e nu_e)/B(B->D mu nu_mu) = 1.020 +/- 0.020stat +/- 0.022sys, and |Vcb| = (39.2 +/- 0.4stat +/- 0.6sys +/- 0.5th)x10^-3.
result:belle-ii-vcb-measurement-2025.why_it_matters: |Vcb| is one of the least precisely known entries of the CKM quark-mixing matrix and a long-standing input to tests of the Standard Model's flavor sector; Belle II's large, clean e+e- data set gives an independent determination from the exclusive B->D l nu channel.

claim.quote: We report the observation of a narrow charmonium-like state produced in the exclusive decay process B+ -> K+ pi+pi- J/psi.

result:belle-x3872-observation-2003.summary_technical: Observation of a narrow state decaying to π⁺π⁻ J/ψ in B⁺ → K⁺ π⁺π⁻ J/ψ, mass 3872.0 ± 0.6(stat) ± 0.5(syst) MeV, very close to the D⁰D̅*⁰ threshold, with a statistical significance in excess of 10σ in 152M BB̅ events.
result:belle-x3872-observation-2003.why_it_matters: First of the 'XYZ' exotic hadrons; its proximity to the D⁰D̅*⁰ threshold drove a generation of work on molecular and tetraquark interpretations.

claim.quote: Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun

result:borexino-cno-evidence-2020.summary_technical: Direct observation, with high statistical significance, of CNO-cycle solar neutrinos, identified as an excess of a few counts per day per 100 t of target above backgrounds in the Borexino liquid-scintillator detector at LNGS — the first experimental evidence of this process.
result:borexino-cno-evidence-2020.why_it_matters: First experimental confirmation that the CNO fusion cycle, thought to dominate energy production in stars more massive than the Sun, actually occurs in stellar cores; also informs the solar metallicity problem.

claim.quote: the first direct spectral measurement of the neutrinos from the keystone proton-proton fusion

notes: result_type set to `measurement` rather than `discovery`/`observation`/`evidence`/`first_detection`: the title and cited quote contain none of the A16 mechanical-check keywords ('discover'/'observ'/'evidence'), and `first_detection` requires 'detect' in the claim quote or a cited source title, which this quote also lacks; the collaboration's own framing (per the fetched summary) is 'the first direct spectral measurement'.
result:borexino-pp-first-detection-2014.summary_technical: First direct spectral measurement of pp-chain solar neutrinos (the reaction producing ~99% of the Sun's power), made with the Borexino liquid-scintillator detector at LNGS.
result:borexino-pp-first-detection-2014.why_it_matters: Completed the direct spectroscopic observation of the dominant solar neutrino-producing reaction, confirming the Sun is currently generating energy at the rate implied by its present-day photon luminosity.

claim.quote: We establish the existence of the top quark using a 67 pb^-1 data sample of Pbar-P collisions at Sqrt(s) = 1.8 TeV collected with the Collider Detector at Fermilab (CDF).

notes: result_type is "observation" (not "discovery") because that is the paper's own title/abstract wording, per instructions to follow the collaboration's wording rather than press characterizations (Fermilab's own tevatron/experiments pages call this "the discovery of the top quark", but the PRL 74, 2626 title and abstract say "Observation ...\"/"We establish the existence...").

title/name corrected in a 2026-09-17 verification pass: the record previously read "Observation of top quark production in ppbar collisions", dropping the published title's "with the Collider Detector at Fermilab" clause and its capitalisation; confirmed verbatim against journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.2626, whose title is "Observation of Top Quark Production in pbar-p Collisions with the Collider Detector at Fermilab" (rendered here with the repository's ASCII "ppbar" convention).
result:cdf-top-quark-observation-1995.summary_technical: CDF observation of top-quark pair production in ppbar collisions at sqrt(s)=1.8 TeV using a 67 pb^-1 sample; a signal consistent with t-tbar -> WWbbbar decay, inconsistent with background by 4.8 sigma, with a corroborating peak in the reconstructed mass distribution.
result:cdf-top-quark-observation-1995.why_it_matters: The top quark was the last of the six quarks of the Standard Model to be found; establishing its existence and mass let physicists test the internal consistency of the Standard Model and, later, constrain the Higgs boson mass.

claim.quote: An excess of events is observed above the expected background, with a local significance of 5.0 standard deviations, at a mass near 125 GeV, signalling the production of a new particle.

notes: The collaboration wording is "observation of a new boson", not "discovery of the Higgs boson"; the identification with the standard model Higgs boson came later.
result:cms-higgs-boson-observation-2012.summary_technical: Combined search in the gamma gamma, ZZ, WW, tau tau and bb channels using up to 5.1 fb^-1 at 7 TeV and 5.3 fb^-1 at 8 TeV; local significance 5.0 sigma at m = 125.3 +/- 0.4 (stat.) +/- 0.5 (syst.) GeV.
result:cms-higgs-boson-observation-2012.why_it_matters: The Higgs boson is the particle associated with the field that gives elementary particles their masses; its observation completed the standard model and opened a new field of precision Higgs measurements.

claim.quote: Here the CMS Collaboration reports the most up-to-date combination of results on the properties of the Higgs boson, including the most stringent limit on the cross section for the production of a pair of Higgs bosons, on the basis of data from proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV.

result:cms-higgs-boson-portrait-2022.summary_technical: Combination of CMS 13 TeV Higgs measurements: production cross sections in all main modes, fermionic and bosonic decay channels, spin-parity, mass, and the most stringent limit at the time on Higgs boson pair production.
result:cms-higgs-boson-portrait-2022.why_it_matters: It is the most complete single-experiment statement of what the Higgs boson is, and the baseline that HL-LHC measurements will be compared against.

claim.quote: The combination of this result with searches by the CMS experiment for H $\to\mathrm{b\overline{b}}$ in other production processes yields an observed (expected) significance of 5.6 (5.5) standard deviations and a signal strength of 1.04 $\pm$ 0.20.

result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.summary_technical: VH production with 41.3 fb^-1 of 2017 data gives 4.8 sigma at m_H = 125.09 GeV; combined with 7, 8 and 13 TeV VH data and with other production modes the observed (expected) significance is 5.6 (5.5) sigma, signal strength 1.04 +/- 0.20.
result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.why_it_matters: H -> bb is the dominant Higgs decay; observing it at the predicted rate confirmed the standard model picture of how the Higgs boson decays.

claim.quote: The combination with the corresponding measurement performed with data collected by the CMS experiment at center-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV leads to an observed significance of 5.9 standard deviations, equal to the expected significance.

result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.summary_technical: 35.9 fb^-1 at 13 TeV gives 4.9 sigma for H -> tau tau; combining with 7 and 8 TeV data gives 5.9 sigma and a signal strength of 1.09 +0.27 -0.26 times the standard model expectation.
result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.why_it_matters: It was the first direct observation of the Higgs boson coupling to fermions by a single experiment, testing whether the Higgs gives mass to matter particles as predicted.

claim.quote: These provide the most stringent lower limits to date on the masses for various spin-1 particles, spin-2 gravitons in the Randall--Sundrum model, as well as spin-1 mediators between the SM and dark matter particles.

notes: Numerical mass limits are quoted in the body of the paper, not in the abstract that was fetched, so no key_value is recorded.
result:cms-high-mass-dilepton-search-202.summary_technical: Dielectron and dimuon mass spectra from up to 140 fb^-1 of 13 TeV data: no significant deviation from the standard model; limits on narrow spin-1 and spin-2 resonances, dark matter mediators, contact interactions and ADD large extra dimensions, plus a TeV-scale test of lepton flavour universality.
result:cms-high-mass-dilepton-search-202.why_it_matters: High-mass dilepton searches are the cleanest and most far-reaching direct probe of new heavy particles at the LHC; the null result constrains many extensions of the standard model at once.

claim.quote: The combined analysis produces the first observation of the $B^0_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ decay, with a statistical significance exceeding six standard deviations, and the best measurement of its branching fraction so far.

notes: A joint CMS + LHCb result. collaboration:lhcb is outside this workstream and is not referenced as an id.
result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2.summary_technical: Joint CMS+LHCb analysis of 7 and 8 TeV data: first observation of B0s -> mu+mu- at >6 sigma, plus 3 sigma evidence for B0 -> mu+mu-; branching fractions compatible with the standard model.
result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2.why_it_matters: The decay is strongly suppressed in the standard model, so its rate is one of the sharpest constraints on new heavy particles in flavour physics.

claim.quote: This is the first observation of such a long-range, near-side feature in two-particle correlation functions in pp or p p-bar collisions.

result:cms-long-range-near-side-correlat.summary_technical: Two-particle Delta(eta)-Delta(phi) correlations in 7 TeV pp collisions show a pronounced near-side ridge at 2.0 < |Delta(eta)| < 4.8 for 1-3 GeV/c tracks in high-multiplicity events (980 nb^-1).
result:cms-long-range-near-side-correlat.why_it_matters: The ridge is a signature previously associated with the quark-gluon plasma; seeing it in proton-proton collisions raised the question of whether collective behaviour also arises in the smallest collision systems.

claim.quote: The top quark mass is measured to be 171.77 $\pm$ 0.37 GeV.

result:cms-top-quark-mass-measurement-20.summary_technical: 36.3 fb^-1 at 13 TeV, lepton+jets ttbar candidates, kinematic fit plus a profile likelihood over up to four observables: m_t = 171.77 +/- 0.37 GeV.
result:cms-top-quark-mass-measurement-20.why_it_matters: The top quark mass enters the electroweak fit and the stability of the Higgs potential, so every improvement in its precision sharpens tests of the standard model.

claim.quote: An excess of events is observed, with a significance of 5.2 standard deviations, over the expectation from the background-only hypothesis.

result:cms-tth-observation-2018.summary_technical: Combination of ttH searches in WW, ZZ, gamma gamma, tau tau and bb final states at 7, 8 and 13 TeV (up to 5.1, 19.7 and 35.9 fb^-1): 5.2 sigma observed, 4.2 sigma expected, signal strength 1.26 +0.31 -0.26.
result:cms-tth-observation-2018.why_it_matters: The top quark Yukawa coupling is the largest in the standard model and is sensitive to new physics; measuring it directly tests the Higgs mechanism where it matters most.

claim.quote: we reach a precise measurement of the W mass, of 80 360.2 ± 9.9 MeV, in agreement with the standard model prediction.

result:cms-w-boson-mass-measurement-2024.summary_technical: W -> mu nu events from 2016 13 TeV data, high-granularity maximum likelihood fit to muon kinematics with in situ constraints on theory inputs: m_W = 80 360.2 +/- 9.9 MeV.
result:cms-w-boson-mass-measurement-2024.why_it_matters: The W and Z masses are related in the standard model, so a precise W mass is a sensitive probe of undiscovered heavy particles entering through quantum loops.

claim.quote: First Measurement of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering on Argon

result:coherent-argon-measurement-2021.summary_technical: First CEvNS measurement on argon using the 22 kg CENNS-10 liquid argon detector; two independent analyses each favor CEvNS over background-only at >3 sigma, with a flux-averaged cross section of (2.2+/-0.7)x10^-39 cm^2 consistent with the Standard Model, and combined with the CsI result to confirm the predicted neutron-number (N^2) scaling.
result:coherent-argon-measurement-2021.why_it_matters: Measuring CEvNS on a second target nucleus (argon, after CsI) tests the Standard Model's predicted N^2 dependence of the cross section on neutron number, directly relevant to the many current and future dark-matter and neutrino experiments that use liquid argon as a target.

claim.quote: Measurement of the Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering Cross Section on CsI by COHERENT
